signals.name: Breadth increase (top decile)
signals.definition: Top cross-sectional decile of the change in the number of 13F managers holding the stock, among managers filing in both quarters, scaled by the number of such managers (Chen, Hong & Stein 2002). Dated at the 45-day filing deadline.
signals.rationale: Broadening ownership signals improving consensus among informed investors.

signals.name: Breadth decrease (bottom decile)
signals.definition: Bottom decile of the same breadth change.

signals.name: Hedge-fund crowd buying
signals.definition: At least 3 concentrated managers opened or increased (>= 25%) the position and buyers exceed sellers by >= 3. Dated at the filing deadline.
signals.rationale: Multiple high-conviction managers accumulating the same stock.

signals.name: Hedge-fund crowd selling
signals.definition: At least 3 concentrated managers exited or cut (>= 25%) and sellers exceed buyers by >= 3.

signals.name: Two-quarter accumulation
signals.definition: Aggregate shares held by concentrated managers rose >= 10% in each of the last two quarters (split-adjusted, same managers).
signals.rationale: Persistent accumulation is harder to explain as noise.

signals.name: New high-conviction position
signals.definition: A concentrated manager discloses a NEW position worth >= 3% of its 13F portfolio. Dated at that manager's own filing date.
signals.rationale: 'Best ideas' of active managers outperform (Cohen, Polk & Silli 2010).

signals.name: Notable fund new position
signals.definition: One of a fixed list of well-known funds (Berkshire, Pershing Square, Appaloosa, …) discloses a new position >= 1% of its portfolio. Dated at its filing date.
signals.rationale: The popular 'clone the gurus' strategy, tested net of the 45-day disclosure lag.
